title: feat(nuxt): unified client prefetch scheduler
body:
### 🔗 Linked issue

follows up on https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/pull/36324

### 📚 Description

we currently prefetch/preload nuxt chunks, components, islands, etc. in an inconsistent way.

| work | before | now |
| --- | --- | --- |
| route chunks (`preloadRouteComponents`) | own 4-slot queue, never cancelled | `route`, cap 4 |
| layout + middleware chunks | unthrottled | `route`, cap 4 |
| `_payload.json` | unthrottled, result discarded after navigating | `payload`, cap 8 |
| island JSON | one `fetch` per island key in the payload | `island`, cap 4 |
| forwarded resource hints | 8 concurrent, 30s timeout | `hint`, cap 8 (unchanged) |
| cross-origin URLs | speculation rules | untouched |

this PR adds one internal scheduler that all of these can now queue onto. now, 'tasks' have:
- **a key** so duplicates are dropped
- **a priority** (as above)
- **a scope** so we can clean up when navigating
- **a group** based on the destination path and query

on navigation we abort in-flight `navigation` work and drop the queue, apart from the payload for the route we're heading to.

previously, we had three different ways of checking for low data; now, we simply hold work in a backlog when `saveData` or 2g is detected, the tab is hidden, or a navigation in progress. (and when any of that changes, we resume it - previously things were just dropped. 😬)

we use the [Prioritized Task Scheduling API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Prioritized_Task_Scheduling_API#browser_compatibility) where possible, so we don't block user input or degrade INP.

however, we don't defer route chunks, nor anything else based on user intent:

| | `prefetchOn: 'visibility'` (default) | `prefetchOn: 'interaction'` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| in view | prefetches | nothing |
| hover / focus | promotes | prefetches |
| pointerdown | promotes | promotes |

promoting moves that destination's queued work to the front of its own priority, so hovering a link prioritises _that_ link's route chunks ahead of other route's, but not ahead of another link's payload.

> [!TIP]
> we now have an experimental dev-only `nuxtApp._prefetch.inspect()` if you want to see what's queued. (we might add a devtools integration for this (cc: @antfu))

the changes here add about 1kB gzipped for an app with pages
